recall_prompt: Say the definition of the adjoint, and give the 2×2 rule.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word TRANSPOSE is the half students drop. The cofactor matrix on its own is not the adjoint.
lines: Let A = [aᵢⱼ] be a square matrix, and let Aᵢⱼ be
the cofactor of the entry aᵢⱼ.
The matrix [Aᵢⱼ] is called the cofactor matrix.
The TRANSPOSE of the cofactor matrix is called
the adjoint of A, and is written Adj A.

recall.must_convey: That the adjoint of A is the TRANSPOSE of the matrix of cofactors of A.
accept: the adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix
form the matrix of cofactors and then transpose it
Adj A equals the cofactor matrix transposed
cofactor matrix ki transpose teeste adjoint vastundi
replace each entry by its cofactor and then take the transpose

steps.why: The adjoint is two moves, not one: cofactors first, then transpose. Leaving the transpose out gives a different matrix, and the identity A(Adj A) = |A| I then fails, which is why the adjoint is defined this way.
common_mistakes: Calling the cofactor matrix itself the adjoint.
Using minors instead of cofactors, so the signs are lost.
Defining the adjoint for a matrix that is not square.
steps.memory_tip: Adjoint is two moves: cofactors first, then transpose.

steps.label: Show it on a 2×2 matrix
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The 2×2 rule is worth quoting: swap the diagonal entries and change the sign of the other two. The identity A(Adj A) = |A| I is the property the adjoint is built for.
lines: For a 2×2 matrix the rule is short:

lines.text: A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{Adj } A = \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}

lines: Swap the two diagonal entries, and change the
For any square A, A(Adj A) = (Adj A)A = |A| I.

recall.must_convey: That for a 2×2 matrix the adjoint swaps the diagonal entries and changes the sign of the other two, and that A(Adj A) = |A| I.
accept: for a two by two matrix swap a and d and change the signs of b and c
Adj of a b c d is d minus b minus c a
A times Adj A equals the determinant times the identity
two by two ki diagonal swap chesi, migilina rendintiki sign marchali
the adjoint times the matrix gives determinant times identity
heard_as: d minus b minus c a

steps.why: The 2×2 case makes the definition concrete in one line, and the identity A(Adj A) = |A| I says what the adjoint is for: divide it by the determinant and the inverse appears.
common_mistakes: Swapping b and c instead of a and d.
Changing the sign of all four entries.
Writing A(Adj A) = I and leaving out the determinant.
steps.memory_tip: For 2×2: swap the diagonal pair, flip the sign of the other pair.
